          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).
- `shards` — CPU docker shards, default `16` (~4 tasks/shard keeps each

Senior Code Reviewer & Security Expert You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,
ci_failures_full.log, pr_discussions.md,
pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}

          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).
- `shards` — CPU docker shards, default `16` (~4 tasks/shard keeps each
  job inside the job window; raise to ~22 for the 89-task 2.x sets).
  Shards run up to 5 in parallel on the default ubuntu runners.

        run: |

              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi

              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).

id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}

          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}

          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).

  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the

              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1

              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).
- `shards` — CPU docker shards, default `16` (~4 tasks/shard keeps each

All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Review Guidelines — evaluate against existing codebase patterns"] G2["Before reviewing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists → READ it — defines coding styles to check against"] G4["Flag deviations from established patterns unless justified in PR description"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 ``` # PR Review General Guidelines ## Review flow ```mermaid flowchart TD START([PR ready for review]) --> READ["1. Read input context:
instruction.md, ticket.md, pr_info.md,
pr_diff.txt, pr_files.txt, ci_failures.md,

pr_discussions_raw.json"] READ --> DIFF["2. Run diff checklist on pr_diff.txt"] DIFF --> FILES["3. Read full content of every changed file"] FILES --> CODEGRAPH["4. Use CodeGraph:
callers/callees of changed symbols,
search for sensitive patterns,
impact analysis"] CODEGRAPH --> DIMS["5. Evaluate review dimensions:
Security · Architecture/OOP · Code quality
Test coverage · Duplication · Backward compatibility"] DIMS --> SEVERITY["6. Classify each finding:
BLOCKING / IMPORTANT / SUGGESTION"] SEVERITY --> EXHAUST["7. Exhaustive pass:
re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Review dimensions Rate the PR across all relevant dimensions: | Dimension | What to check | |---|---| | **Security** | injection, unsafe interpolation, secret leakage, missing permissions, unsafe defaults | | **Architecture / OOP** | SRP, coupling, abstraction consistency, provider/repository boundaries | | **Code quality** | naming, complexity, error handling, logging, comments | | **Tests** | coverage for new/changed paths, meaningful assertions, no brittle string-only tests | | **Duplication** | copy-paste, duplicated logic across files, duplicated configuration | | **Backward compatibility** | public API changes, migration paths, default behavior | | **Performance** | unnecessary rebuilds, heavy sync operations, missing timeouts | | **Workflow / CI safety** | (when `.github/workflows/` changes) secret declarations, ref pinning, permissions, timeouts | ## 6. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. Outputs Write the standard review artifacts: - `outputs/pr_review.json` — structured data with `recommendation`, `summary`, `inlineComments`, `issueCounts` - `outputs/pr_review_general.md` — 1-2 paragraph general PR comment - `outputs/pr_review_comments/*.md` — one file per detailed inline comment **Inline comment lines must be present in the PR diff.** GitHub review threads can only be attached to added or context lines inside a diff hunk. If `pr_diff.txt` is truncated, run `git diff origin/{baseBranch}...HEAD` to locate the correct line numbers. Findings on unchanged code outside the diff belong in `outputs/pr_review_general.md`, not as inline comments. Do NOT write `outputs/response.md`; the review is posted to GitHub only. ```mermaid flowchart TD O1["Write outputs/pr_review.json — structured data for GitHub PR review…

id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the

- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).

              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'

              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then

              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From

              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0

              ;;

              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")

              ;;

              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new

              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY

              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.

blocks.text:
Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).
- `shards` — CPU docker shards, default `16` (~4 tasks/shard keeps each

id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the

- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).

              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1

              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the

              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the
  `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY` secret.
- `attempts` — harbor `-k` trials per task, default `5` (leaderboard protocol).
- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).
- `shards` — CPU docker shards, default `16` (~4 tasks/shard keeps each
  job inside the job window; raise to ~22 for the 89-task 2.x sets).

## Automated Code Review — REQUEST_CHANGES

**Summary**: The `kimi-for-coding` model-id correction is correct and the 83 terminal-bench tests pass locally, but the byte-consistent mirror in `bench-harbor.yml` was not updated — this deterministically breaks `test_resolve_block_is_byte_consistent_with_bench_yml` and leaves the exact wrong-id bug this PR fixes live on the harbor bench path.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 The harbor resolve step (`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml:188`) still sets `model='k3-256k'` and `run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"`. `bench-harbor.yml:30` declares an explicit sync contract ("keep both in sync — cross-reference comment in both files"), enforced by `test_resolve_block_is_byte_consistent_with_bench_yml` — which now fails (verified locally: 39 harbor tests, 1 failure). Note this suite only runs on `workflow_dispatch` of Bench Harbor, so PR CI stays green while the invariant is broken; a kimi harbor dispatch would also send the wrong model id.

**Next Steps**:
1. Mirror the correction into `bench-harbor.yml` (model, label, and comment lines) so the resolve blocks stay byte-identical, and update the stale assertions in `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py:259-263` and `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py:76-83`.
2. 💡 `docs/bench.md:75` still documents `kimi-for-coding` as `` `k3-256k` `` — update with the same owner correction.
3. 💡 Optional: `bench/pricing.json` lost the `k3-256k` key, so re-rendering the summary of the first kimi run (38068865372) will now report it as unpriced — acceptable if historical re-renders aren't a concern.

🚨 **BLOCKING: byte-consistent harbor mirror not updated — repo sync invariant broken**

The terminal-bench correction here is right, but the same resolve step exists as a declared byte-identical copy in `.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml` (gh-1503 port, merged via #1505). That file still has:

```bash
model='k3-256k'
run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
```

Two concrete problems:

1. **A test fails on this branch right now.** `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py::HarborProviderResolveStepTest::test_resolve_block_is_byte_consistent_with_bench_yml` asserts the two resolve blocks are byte-identical ("a drifted copy would silently diverge the two bench paths"). Verified locally: the harbor suite is 39 tests with **1 failure** after this change. The PR's "83/83 green" only covers `bench/terminal_bench` — and because `bench-harbor.yml` is `workflow_dispatch`-only, PR CI will not catch this; it fires on the next harbor dispatch.

2. **The bug this PR fixes stays live on the harbor path.** A `provider=kimi-for-coding` Bench Harbor dispatch would send `model='k3-256k'` to `https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1` — the same wrong id the owner correction here disproves.

Fix: apply the identical correction to `bench-harbor.yml` (same comment lines too, to preserve byte-consistency), and update the stale kimi assertions in `bench/harbor_fa/test_bench_harbor_workflow.py:259-263` and `bench/harbor_fa/test_summary.py:76-83`. re-read changed files,
surface ALL remaining issues"] EXHAUST --> OUTPUT["8. Write outputs:
pr_review.json · pr_review_general.md · pr_review_comments/*.md"] OUTPUT --> END([End]) ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Read the full content of every changed file: - imports and dependencies - class/method responsibilities and adherence to SRP / OOP principles - naming consistency with the rest of the codebase - error handling, logging, and edge cases - test coverage for changed behavior - backward-compatibility and migration impact ## 4. Impact analysis (CodeGraph or grep fallback) Use CodeGraph to find "what could break": - `codegraph_callers` / `codegraph_callees` on modified public symbols - `codegraph_search` for: `PAT_TOKEN`, `secrets.`, `github.token`, `previousViewModel` - `codegraph_impact` before flagging architectural changes **If CodeGraph unavailable**, use grep and document it: ```bash grep -rn "changedFunctionName" --include="*.ts" . grep -rn "secrets\.\|github\.token" . ``` ## 5. Severity classification Classify every finding before writing outputs: - **BLOCKING** — merge would cause a bug, security issue, data loss, or CI break. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              # The model id IS the plan name (owner correction, gh-1471
              # follow-up): the coding endpoint serves it as
              # 'kimi-for-coding', not k3-256k.
              model='kimi-for-coding'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # model == choice by construction — no doubled label.
              run_label="kimi-for-coding"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts. From
              # here down the checks mirror the Dart env preconfig's
              # consumer contract (lib/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart)
              # so a bad dispatch burns one setup minute, never
              # shard-hours failing loud inside every trial.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

Dispatch **Bench Harbor** (`workflow_dispatch`). Inputs:

- `dataset` — family label (`2.0`/`2.1`/`3.0`/`4.0`), a bare version
  (`4.0.0`), or a full Harbor id; default
  `terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest` (the 2.1 family — issue
  #1316 migrated the default dispatch from 4.0 to Terminal-Bench 2.x).
- `tasks` — comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset. Empty = the full
  dataset (size per family above). The family smoke task is the
  one-task check.
- `confirm-full-run` — must be `true` for a full (tasks-less) run of an
  intermediate family (2.0/2.1/3.0); a full family sweep is hours of GPU
  + LLM spend. Smoke runs and 4.0 are unaffected (the historical 4.0
  default dispatch keeps its no-confirmation behaviour).
- `provider` — `zai-glm-5.3-flash` (default; byte-identical to the
  pre-gh-1503 wiring), `kimi-for-coding` (`k3-256k`, needs the
  `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` secret), or `custom` (needs `FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY`
  + `provider-config`). Same contract as the legacy bench's gh-1471
  provider selection — the model is derived from the provider, so the
  old free-text `model` input is gone (gh-1503).
- `provider-config` — ONLY when `provider=custom`: the provider config
  JSON `{"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`. The
  API key never rides this input — it comes only from the

- `n-concurrent` — default `1` (z.ai rate limits; the kimi coding plan
  tolerates more — the owner picks the level at dispatch).

- Read the full diff (bench.yml resolve step, `bench/pricing.json` rekey, two test files) and the complete changed files plus their mirrors.

`.github/workflows/bench-harbor.yml:188` — the gh-1503 port copied the gh-1471 resolve step as a **declared byte-identical mirror** ("keep both in sync — cross-reference comment in both files"). This PR updates `bench.yml` but not the mirror, which:

2. **Leaves the exact bug this PR fixes live** on the harbor path: a `provider=kimi-for-coding` harbor dispatch still sends `model='k3-256k'`, plus its tests (`test_bench_harbor_workflow.py:259-263`, `test_summary.py:76-83`) assert the wrong value, and `docs/bench.md:75` still documents the old id.

The inline comment anchors to `bench.yml:228` (a line in the diff), since the harbor file itself isn't part of the diff.

### What's fine
The correction itself (model id = plan name), the label collapse, the pricing rekey (lookup is by model name via `fa_usage.price_entry`, so the new key is consistent), and the zai default byte-identity (REG-1) are all sound; no secrets/permissions/scope issues in the changed hunks.
